title: acme-cloud, mapped
subtitle: What runs for Acme Tickets, what the internet can reach, and where code and deployment differ.

verdict.text: Acme Tickets is one Azure subscription in `westeurope`: a .NET portal on App Service, a queue worker on an internal Container Apps environment, one SQL database, and a reports part deployed with Bicep, plus a Redis cache only the deployment knows about. By the code the internet can reach the SQL server from any address through a rule named temporary, read the reports `exports` container without signing in, and call a reports API with no sign-in in the code, and the first two should not be open.

flows.title: A customer buys a ticket: portal to the database

steps.text: The browser looks up `www.tickets.example.com`. The CNAME points at the portal's default hostname (`record`, main.tf:37) [high]. The code binds no custom hostname to the app, so this name may not serve the portal [med].
HTTPS only, TLS 1.2 minimum (`https_only`, app.tf:17; `minimum_tls_version`, app.tf:21) [high]. Nothing stands in front of it: no WAF and no access restrictions in the code.

`SQL_SERVER` gives the server name (app.tf:30). The code has no SQL private endpoint and no VNet rule, so the connection goes to the public endpoint [high]. The only rule in the code that admits it is `allow-all-temporary` (data.tf:21).

`db-tickets`, `GP_Gen5_2`, 100 GB, not zone redundant (data.tf:12-18) [high]. That the portal queries this database is inferred from the setting: the application code is not here [med]. How it signs in is unknown: no identity and no connection string in the code.

flows.title: The portal stores a ticket file in the private account

steps.text: `TICKET_STORAGE` is the blob endpoint (app.tf:31). VNet integration on `snet-app` (`virtual_network_subnet_id`, app.tf:18) gives the portal a way to the private endpoint in `snet-data` (data.tf:78) [high]. **Gap:** neither the code nor the export has a private DNS zone, so the blob name resolves to the public address [med], where public access is off.

The private endpoint for `blob` (data.tf:87) leads into the account. `public_network_access_enabled = false` (data.tf:35) and no anonymous access (data.tf:36) [high]. With the DNS gap above this path may not work at all [med]. The Key Vault has the same private-endpoint shape and the same gap (data.tf:64).

flows.title: Queued work: emails and seat holds

steps.text: `SERVICEBUS_NAMESPACE` (app.tf:32) names the namespace; the queues are `ticket-emails` and `seat-holds` (messaging.tf:12) [high]. Which queue it writes to is not stated. **Gap:** `local_auth_enabled = false` (messaging.tf:7) allows Entra ID only, and the portal has no identity, so the code gives it no way to sign in [med].

The worker gets the same namespace (`SERVICEBUS_NAMESPACE`, modules/worker/main.tf:53) and a system-assigned identity (main.tf:39) [high]. It pulls outward, so nothing calls it: no ingress and an internal environment (app.tf:46) [high]. **Gap:** no role assignment in the code; `principal_id` is output and never used (modules/worker/main.tf:60) [high].
`external: true`, target port 8080 (reports.bicep:50-51) [high]. No sign-in in the Bicep and no VNet on the environment (reports.bicep:32-38) [med].

`REPORTS_STORAGE` holds the account name (reports.bicep:65-66) [high]. That the API reads the `exports` container is inferred from the file's first comment (reports.bicep:1) [med]. No role assignment in the code, so how it signs in is unknown.

The same files can be fetched directly, without the API: `allowBlobPublicAccess: true` (reports.bicep:13) and `publicAccess: 'Blob'` on `exports` (reports.bicep:28) allow anonymous reads of any blob whose URL is known [high].

sections.title: What could not be read
sections.intro: The first four rows are what the script could not follow; each was opened by hand. The rest are gaps the script does not report.

rows: Opened: `toset` of two literal names, so 2 queues. Whether they exist today is not in the export.
Opened: `each.value` is `ticket-emails` and `seat-holds`. Nothing stays unknown.
The name ends in `random_string.suffix.result`, known only from state, which was not opened. The export candidate fits but does not prove it [med].
Opened: `www` in `tickets.example.com`, to the portal's default hostname. Not confirmed deployed, and no hostname binding on the app in the code.
No role assignment in the code, and the export cannot list them. Who may use Key Vault, Service Bus, storage and SQL stays unknown.
Not a resource in the code and not in the export. Its subscription, and how images are pulled, stay unknown.
What the portal, worker and reports API actually call, which queue each uses and how each signs in. Every request link is inferred from settings.
No `backend` block, and state files are git-ignored: where the state lives is unknown. No state or variable file was opened.

blocks.title: Assumed, because no questions were asked
items: The export of 2026-11-08 is taken as the deployed state; anything newer is not seen.
Names are computed from the variable defaults (`environment = prod`, `location = westeurope`): no tfvars or parameter files were read.
A setting not written in the code is taken at its Azure default: public access on for SQL, App Service and Storage, no network rules on Storage [med].
`stacmeticketsqx7k2p` is treated as the Terraform ticket account [med].
The portal and the worker are drawn as using what their settings name. The settings were read; the requests were not observed.
The Bicep's resources are drawn in the same subscription because the export places them there.
Is `allow-all-temporary` still applied? It was added for a load test on 2026-07-14. Before removing it, the portal needs another way in: it is the only rule in the code that admits the portal [med].
What is in the `exports` container? It is readable without signing in, and the README says customer data stays in the EU.
Who created `redis-acme-sessions-prod`, what uses it, and what is its network setting? The README says changes go through this repository.
Was `stacmebackupsprod` never applied, or removed? Nothing in the code writes to it, so where do backups go?
`SMTP_PASSWORD` is a literal in the code (app.tf:34) and so in the git history. Against the README's Key Vault rule; should it be rotated and moved?
How does the portal sign in to Key Vault and Service Bus? It has no identity, the vault uses RBAC, and Service Bus accepts Entra ID only.
Where do the worker's and the reports API's permissions come from? No role assignment is in the code, and the worker's `principal_id` output is unused.
Is there a private DNS zone outside this subscription? Without one the private endpoints are not found by name from the portal [med].
Does `www.tickets.example.com` work? There is a CNAME, but no hostname binding or certificate in the code.
Should Application Insights be wired to the portal, and should any alert use `ag-acme-tickets-prod`? Neither is connected in code or export.
Where is the Terraform state, and who runs it? `variables.tf` says the SQL password is set from a pipeline, the README says laptops, and there is no backend block.
